problems.fix: eng-tolerancing skill: a bearing-seat paragraph for light-alloy housings: 'aluminium housing at +50 K opens the seat by about alpha-difference x D x dT (about 30 um at 52 mm): choose a tighter housing class (K7/M7), compute the hot range, do not move to H7'. what_worked: Loaded eng-toolkit and eng-tolerancing before its first tool call, eng-plot-results before the chart; asked the right missing questions for the stack-up (chain, spec, temperature, groove location) rather than computing blind.
Explained plainly that the ISO table H7/k5 is not the bearing's fit and computed -21..-2 um for k5 against the 0/-10 bore (labelled own arithmetic, recalled bore).

Stack-up: used metrology_stackup_1d with Monte Carlo, quoted result_mean 0.44 (not the nominal 0.30), gave the worst-case verdict 'not OK' and a fix verified by the tool (0.15..0.48, 1,000,000 samples, 0 outside), and said the spacer nominal change is the person's decision.
Re-asked where the groove is when the temperature effect depended on it, and dropped the aluminium assumption when told it is on the steel shaft.
